afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 281036
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
336 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather will prevail through early next week 
  with temperatures hovering slightly above normal for late 
  November.

- A Pacific low is expected to track through the Desert Southwest
  during the middle of next week, leading to a period with 
  widespread gusty winds, rain chances, and cooler temperatures.

- Isolated or embedded thunderstorms, some strong, may be 
  possible with this Pacific low, especially ahead of the initial 
  cold front Tuesday into Tuesday night.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH MONDAY/... 
A period of dry and tranquil weather will prevail through the 
beginning of the upcoming work week, as anticyclonic flow aloft 
transitions to quasi-zonal. Several shortwaves/upper lows will 
conspire to flatten the midlevel anticyclone in place just west of
the region as they overtop the feature. As a result, midlevel 
heights will continue to decrease through Monday, dropping from 
current RAP analyzed H5 heights of 584-588 dam closer to 574-576 
dam, near the median of climatology. However, forecast surface 
temperatures are somewhat decoupled from the midlevel heights and 
will be more so driven by cloud cover this weekend. Abundant high 
clouds today will prevent us from realizing much above normal 
afternoon temperatures, and instead, we can expect a continuation 
of lower desert highs in the middle to upper 70s. It will be a 
similar story Sunday, but slightly lower coverage of clouds will 
allow temperatures to warm a few degrees further, peaking near 80F
for the typically warmer lower desert locales. This is as much as
7F-10F above daily normals, but still at least ~5F below record 
highs. Finally by Monday, lower level thermal profiles will cool 
closer to seasonal averages (NAEFS/ENS mean 850 mb temperatures 
around 11C-13C). However, sunny skies will make for a rather 
stable temperature forecast even on Monday, nearly identical to 
forecast highs/lows today or perhaps a few degrees cooler in some 
places.

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...    
On Tuesday, attention turns to a significant Pacific low that will 
develop off the SoCal/Northern Baja Coast early in the week and 
progress through the Desert Southwest during the middle of the week. 
Ensembles are in good agreement that a potent PV anomaly will 
rapidly dive south from the vicinity of the Aleutian Islands riding 
a meridional jet streak late this weekend into early this upcoming 
work week. This will fill the base of a deep, progressive Pacific 
trough Monday night. Ensemble mean SLP just offshore will bottom out 
near climatological minimums for this time of year because of how 
far south this system is expected to dig. NAEFS mean H5 heights are 
also near or just below the 1st percentile of climatology at the 
center of the upper low as it develops.

Ahead of this Pacific low, ensembles have started to hone in on a 
plume of high IVT, consistent with an inland penetrating AR, 
developing and rapidly moistening the column over the forecast area. 
IVT values upwards of 300-500 kg/(ms) are now shown in the NAEFS 
mean, in excess of the 99th percentile of climatology. However, this 
period of excellent moisture transport will be relatively short 
lived as the initial Pacific front sweeps west to east across the 
forecast area Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday night. Tracking with 
this initial plume of moisture, rain chances will begin at first for 
portions of Southeast CA and Southwest AZ Tuesday morning into the 
afternoon and then spread into South-Central AZ likely by Tuesday 
evening. Details are becoming more clear on the potential for 
embedded thunderstorms ahead of this initial front. Destabilization 
now seems like it will be sufficient, with model soundings showing 
MUCAPEs peaking around 500-750 J/kg. This coupled with strong wind 
shear (EBWD upwards of 30-35 kts) may even support some strong to 
marginally severe storms. The prevalence of thunderstorms will also 
determine whether locally heavy rain and flash flooding becomes a 
concern, however, fast storm motion should act to reduce this 
threat. On Wednesday, the core of the upper low will finally 
progress through the region. GFS/ECMWF continue to show a similar 
evolution where the center of this low passes somewhere over/near 
the forecast area and brings yet another period of more widespread 
showers before passing east in the evening. Shower activity will 
slowly trail off over the higher terrain of Eastern AZ Wednesday 
night. Guidance has once again come in with higher event-total 
rainfall in the latest iterations. Average forecast rain totals from 
the latest WPC QPF are now between 1.00-1.50" across the South-
Central AZ lower deserts, with higher totals near or in excess of 
2.00" over the high terrain just north and east of the Greater 
Phoenix Area. The lower deserts of Southeast CA and far Southwest AZ 
will suffer from rain shadowing effects, with average forecast 
totals generally between 0.25-1.00". Locally higher totals will be 
possible in thunderstorms. As a result of this impactful amount of 
forecast precipitation, WPC has hoisted a Slight risk for excessive 
rainfall across almost all of the CWA on Day 4 (12Z Tuesday - 12Z 
Wednesday). 

The other major concern with this system will be strong gradient 
winds. The quick deepening and progressive nature of this system 
will result in considerable height packing over the region, 
inducing a deep southwesterly jet over AZ. The current timing of 
this system and model soundings suggest that there will be a 
period of clear skies coinciding with the strongest flow aloft. 
NAEFS mean 850-700 mb wind speeds peak upwards of 40-45 kts, 
around the 98th-99th percentiles of climatology during the 
afternoon Tuesday. Under mostly sunny skies, this higher momentum 
air could mix down to the surface, resulting in widespread gusts 
of 30-50 mph. At this time, in seems the jet of stronger winds 
aloft will skip over Southeast CA, and so forecast peak gusts 
there are not quite as high. If there is little change in this 
forecast as we get closer to event, Wind Advisories will likely be
needed for much of the CWA from the Lower CO River Valley 
eastward. 

By Thursday, the Pacific low will have weakened substantially and 
progressed east of the region, allowing an opportunity for quick 
clearing and a period with weak temperature/pressure gradients 
across the region. Light winds and widespread wetting rainfall from 
the night before could set the stage for fog to develop across 
portions of the lower deserts, but this will be highly dependent on 
cloud cover. Regardless, cooler temperatures behind the front will 
prevail starting Wednesday, with latest NBM showing temperatures 
dropping close to daily normals. Quieter weather should follow the 
passage of this Pacific trough as a period of transient ridging 
takes hold. Model consensus by next weekend is for an active pattern 
to take hold with mean troughing establishing over the Western CONUS 
and a series of upper lows/shortwave troughs progressing through the 
region. Periodic precipitation chances, elevated winds, and 
continued cooler temperatures seem like the theme from that point 
onward.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0525Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT;
Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

No aviation weather concerns are expected during the TAF period.
Light winds (aob 10 kt) will follow their typical diurnal 
patterns, with extended periods of variable to calm conditions. 
SCT-BKN high cirrus clouds will be common throughout the TAF 
period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and generally tranquil conditions will prevail through the
beginning of next week. Temperatures will be fairly stable during
this time in a 3F-10F above normal range. Afternoon minimum 
humidities will vary between 15-25% areawide following fair to 
good overnight recoveries between 30-60% through the weekend.
Humidity will then increase Monday through the middle of next week
as a Pacific low approaches and tracks over the area. This system
will result in increasing southerly to southwesterly winds, 
especially by Tuesday, and widespread chances for wetting rain.
Embedded thunderstorms are possible, especially on Tuesday ahead
of the initial cold front. Until then, anticipate winds to be 
light, mostly below 15 mph.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Updated 11/28 1030Z.
Gila River: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock 
Dam through the Dateland area due to continued flow in the Gila 
River, however, upstream releases have ceased. Water levels near 
Dateland have begun to decrease, with gauge data now showing a 
stage of 5 ft and flow around 150 cfs. A separate Flood Warning 
segment remains in effect from Dateland to Yuma. These water 
levels will have the potential to flood farm fields and low water 
crossings along the river downstream from the dam. The downstream 
gauge near Dome has yet to respond. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Whittock
AVIATION...Berislavich
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock
HYDROLOGY...Whittock
